findings.note: Senate bill 320 of the 187th General Court, 'An Act relative to voter identification.', filed by Bruce E. Tarr with other Senate petitioners. Referred to the Joint Committee on Election Laws on 1/24/2011. A hearing was scheduled for 9/21/2011. It was accompanied by a study order (S2364). The page does not show the bill text in the saved view.

Senate bill 339 of the 188th General Court, 'An Act relative to voter identification.', filed by Bruce E. Tarr with two co-petitioners. Referred to the committee on Election Laws on 1/22/2013. A hearing was scheduled for 12/04/2013. It was accompanied by a study order (H4145).

Senate bill 1273 of the 194th General Court, 'legislation relative the power of courts and judges to maintain election integrity', filed by Bruce E. Tarr and sent to the Judiciary committee. A hearing was scheduled for 6/03/2025. Related to election integrity in general; the listing does not mention ID.

Tarr presented S.320, An Act relative to voter identification. It would require a voter at the polls to show identification, such as a social security card or another pre-printed form that gives the name and either address, signature or photograph.

Tarr presented S.339, An Act relative to voter identification, with two co-petitioners. Same wording as S.320: the voter shows identification such as a social security card or other pre-printed form with name and address, signature or photograph.
Tarr is listed as a petitioner on S.335, An Act requiring photo identification to receive a ballot (presented by another senator). Date is the Senate docket filing date shown on the bill's HTML page.
subjects: photo ID to receive a ballot

findings.note: Tarr is listed as a petitioner on S.378, An Act establishing voter identification procedures. A voter would be told to show a Massachusetts driver's license, state photo ID card, U.S. passport or Social Security card; a person without the required ID would not be permitted to vote.

Tarr is listed as a petitioner on S.389, An Act requiring photo identification to receive a ballot. Valid photo IDs: Massachusetts driver's license, U.S. passport, student ID or Massachusetts ID card; a Massachusetts ID card would be issued at no cost.
subjects: photo ID to receive a ballot

findings.motion: Amendment S2545-44 (filed by Tarr and O'Connor): photo ID at the polls with affidavit option, and free ID process for homeless or indigent people
findings.note: Amendment to the 2022 Senate driver's license bill draft. Voters must show government-issued or tribal photo ID; a person without it may sign an affidavit and then receive a ballot. Also requires a process for homeless or indigent people to get a state ID with fees waived. The amendment page shows no date; month taken from the Senate debate week reported by Boston 25 on 2022-05-05.
